lessonTitle: 37. n-th roots of a complex number
lessonTitleEnglish: n-th roots of a complex number
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 10 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: A nonzero complex number has exactly n n-th roots: the n-th root of r times (cos((α + 2πk)/n) + i sin((α + 2πk)/n)), k = 0, ..., n − 1.
stages.headlineEnglish: A nonzero complex number has exactly n n-th roots: the n-th root of r times (cos((α + 2πk)/n) + i sin((α + 2πk)/n)), k = 0, ..., n − 1.

stages.headline: The roots lie on a circle of radius ⁿ√r and form a regular n-gon; the cube roots of 1 are 1 and −1/2 ± (√3/2)i.
stages.headlineEnglish: The roots lie on a circle of radius ⁿ√r and form a regular n-gon; the cube roots of 1 are 1 and −1/2 ± (√3/2)i.

stages.headline: Example: 2i = 2(cos π/2 + i sin π/2); its square roots are √2(cos π/4 + i sin π/4) = 1 + i and −1 − i.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: 2i = 2(cos π/2 + i sin π/2); its square roots are √2(cos π/4 + i sin π/4) = 1 + i and −1 − i.
